content:
More than 400 trick-or-treat stops are already registered in Nuevo Laredo on the Dulce Halloween app, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo — a live map of decorated houses and businesses handing out candy for tonight, October 31.

Dulce Halloween is a free app for iOS and Android that shows, in real time, which homes are actively giving out candy. Neighbors mark their house on the map, and a pumpkin icon signals the stop is live; when the candy runs out, the pin goes dark. Families can check hours and photos of decorations before heading out, and plan a route instead of wandering block to block.

The platform reports more than 100,000 registered houses across Mexico and the United States, and Nuevo Laredo's 400-plus points put the city firmly on the map for Halloween night.

The idea is simple: fewer empty porches, fewer wasted walks, and a route families can plan together before dark. As with any Halloween outing, the map works best paired with the basics — stay on lit streets, go in groups, and check that a stop is still marked active before walking over.

Why it matters

Halloween in Nuevo Laredo is a neighborhood event, and this year the neighborhood organized itself on a map. Four hundred registered stops is not just a number — it is hundreds of households that signed up to welcome trick-or-treaters tonight.
